title: Rav Ovadiah
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Berakhot 15a has him reciting before Rava. Niddah 20b relates that Ifra Hormiz, King Shapur’s mother, sent blood to Rava. Rav Ovadiah was sitting before him; he smelled it and said, “This is blood of desire.” The plain sense is that Rava smelled it, but Yuchasin takes the subject to be Rav Ovadiah. Seder HaDorot says that Yuchasin erred; yet this is also the Rashba’s view in Niddah: “It seems to me that Rav Ovadiah smelled it, for Rava was not expert in blood.” He develops the argument at length there.
And in Bava Batra 22b, Rava permitted Rav Yoshiyah and Rav Ovadiah the marketplace.

notes.text: The verb means “smelled it,” not “was on his way.” Whether Rava or Ovadiah smelled the blood is exactly the disagreement Hyman reports; the English keeps that disagreement visible.

The consulted Niddah 20b has Ovadiah seated before Rava in the Ifra Hormiz blood episode, distinct from the adjacent Rabbi Elazar/Ami episode. Rashba on Niddah 20b, Gerlitz edition published by Oraita, explicitly argues that Ovadiah smelled the blood and that Rava was not expert in blood. Hyman’s plain-sense Rava reading and reported disagreement remain visible; Yuchasin and Seder HaDorot exact editions were not inspected here.
